label: r4c1
name: Flip-only, 64 envs
hypothesis: Halve n_envs to 64 with 8 minibatches (128 samples each, as in r3c2). Samples stay the same, but there are about 120 policy updates instead of 60. Doubling the updates raised the mean from 0.64 to 0.89, and the curve was still rising, so doubling again should improve sample use. Refuted if the mean falls below about 0.85 or a seed collapses, which would mean the updates have become too noisy.
last_analysis: Two things clearly mattered. First, the flip: running the network in the agent's own mirrored action frame (flip-only) was needed for any success, while learned axis-mixing failed. Second, more frequent updates: r3c2 has the same samples as r2c1 but twice as many policy updates, and it scored 0.89 with both seeds high (0.88 and 0.91). r2c1 scored 0.64 with seeds 0.84 and 0.43. Every run that lost samples or got noisier did worse: the deeper trunk, the cheap recipe with high entropy, and 3 epochs on the flip-concat network. Small output initialisation and gamma 0.99 gave nothing clear. In r3c2 the learning curve was still rising at the end (0.85 training success). This is the last round, so the safest gains are recipe refinements of r3c2 along the axis that worked: more, smaller updates. One candidate also tests more samples per update through extra epochs. I keep the architecture fixed so that each result is easy to read.
